indiaChemicals.value: Indian chemical industry estimated at USD 155-165 bn, projected USD 230-255 bn by 2030 (~8-9% CAGR); global chemicals expected to grow 3-4% (ACC/ICCA)

chinaOvercapacity.value: China's capacity additions drove overcapacity, intense competition and margin compression in commodity and bulk chemicals; Aarti's gross margin fell from 42% (FY23) to 34% (9MFY26) vs a ~45% decadal average; blended realisations −25% in FY26

timeline.what: US penalty tariff on India to 50% (about half of Aarti's US sales exempt; PDA chain hit hardest)
China 'anti-involution' drive and reversal of export incentives
India-US trade deal announced: tariff on Indian goods ~18% vs ~34% for China (India Ratings)
West Asia conflict: crude-linked raw materials spike; Middle East fuel-additive exports halted; freight up
China removes export VAT rebates on major NCB-chain products; NCB margins recover

fuelAdditives.value: Demand driven by the gasoline-naphtha crack ($15-18/bbl in Q1FY27, 'healthy'); the global fuel-additive market is 'in millions of tons' (MMA capacity well under 1 mn t vs >30 mn t of MTBE, per older calls); seasonal weakness Oct-Dec; competition from 2-3 Indian and 2-3 Chinese makers

capacityRationalisation.value: CEO: significant rationalisation of chemical capacity in Europe and North-East Asia and slower Chinese additions could restructure industry margins 'post 28, 29', but 'we have to wait at least 2 or 3 more years'

sectorDerating.value: On 30-Sep-2026, specialty-chemical peers traded 14-44% below their post-Apr-2023 median EV/EBITDA (median ~−31%) and 21-49% below their median P/E; Aarti −18% (EV/EBITDA) and −22% (P/E)
sectorDerating.src: Screener.in multiples at the NSE close on 30-Sep-2026 (GAM calculation)

peersNote: Deepak Nitrite (closest: nitration/phenol, NT competitor), Atul (diversified benzene/aromatics), Vinati (ATBS/IBB), Navin Fluorine and SRF (fluorochemicals, CDMO), Clean Science, Laxmi Organic (acetyls), Alkyl Amines (amines; standalone basis). No listed peer has Aarti's mix of benzene chains plus a fuel-additive business; Chinese producers are the real competitors.

moat.dimension: Scale and integration in benzene chains

Gross margin 42% → 34% (FY23 → 9MFY26) as Chinese supply set prices; blended realisations −25% in FY26
No customer ≥10%; majority of FY25 revenue from 10-year+ relationships; repeat contract from a global major (Mar-2026); ~30-40% of business contractual (2024)
Continuous nitration; but CEO concedes a 'technological disadvantage' in PDA; NT margins hit by isomer imbalance
Market leader, top-decile cost, but 2-3 Indian and 2-3 Chinese competitors and a commodity-like spread business tied to gasoline cracks
Net debt 3.65x EBITDA; CRISIL and India Ratings outlooks Negative
ROCE 22% (FY22) → 7% (FY26); Zone IV ~1.5-2 years late; FY24-25 EBITDA guidance missed by 29-41%

conflicts: FY22 EBITDA: company reported ₹1,930 cr incl. ₹631 cr termination fee (₹1,320 cr ex-fee, incl. pharma; restated chemicals-only ₹919 cr) vs Screener ₹1,720 cr. We avoid FY22 comparisons where possible.
Company EBITDA vs Screener: FY24 ₹984 vs ₹978 cr; FY25 ₹1,016 (also ₹1,014 in the MD&A) vs ₹997 cr; FY26 ₹1,172 vs ₹1,168 cr. The model uses Screener.
FY26 capex: company ₹1,125 cr vs CRISIL ₹1,179 cr.
Fuel-additive capacity: CRISIL says 360 kTPA reached in Jul-2026; the AR (27-Aug-2026) still calls it 'underway'. The Q1FY27 presentation confirms completion in Jul-2026.
Augene JV partner: described as UPL in Aug-2024; named Superform (Chemistries) from 2025-26 (AR26 calls it a UPL subsidiary). Steady-state revenue ₹400-500 cr (Aug-2024) vs ₹300-400 cr (2026).
Zone IV delay: 3-4 months (May-2026) vs 2 quarters (Jul-2026 presentation) vs 3-6 months (Jul-2026 call); the AR's CWIP note says no project is overdue at Mar-26.
